\title{Parallax Correction of INSAT-3DR Imagery Over India: An Open-Source Tool and the Limits of Validation Against GPM Radar}

\author{Naveen~Bapalli%
\thanks{N. Bapalli is an independent researcher, India (e-mail: [to be added]).}}

\markboth{Manuscript draft, \today}{Bapalli: Parallax Correction of INSAT-3DR Imagery Over India}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Geostationary imagers see high clouds displaced away from the sub-satellite point. For INSAT-3DR at 74\textdegree\,E, deep convection over the Himalaya and Northeast India appears about 10\,km from its true position. We present PyGeoParallax-IN, an open-source tool that corrects this parallax by tracing each line of sight to the cloud top on the WGS84 ellipsoid, with optional terrain and a coastline-based navigation correction, and that produces uncorrected and corrected datasets on a common grid. Against GPM Ku-band radar in 38 usable monsoon cases (2018--2024), the correction moves deep cores by 4--10\,km along the line of sight and leaves the cross-look offset unchanged. It reverses the mean storm-scale bias ($+2.2$ to $-1.9$\,km), but the per-case gain is not significant. At convective cores, uncorrected cold cores already coincide with GPM deep-echo cells, and only about 5\,\% of the computed parallax is visible. A navigation correction fitted to GPM centres the cells but degrades the storm-scale agreement; no single translation centres both measures, which differ by 2--5\,km. We attribute this mainly to storm structure, which limits GPM-based validation of absolute position to about $\pm$3--5\,km. INSAT-3DR navigation errors are seasonal, 7--20\,km westward in winter. A precipitation-type U-Net retrained on corrected input does not improve, and its convective scores fall slightly.
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
Geostationary satellites, INSAT-3DR, parallax correction, image navigation, Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM), radar validation, monsoon convection, open-source software.
\end{IEEEkeywords}

\section*{Code and Data Availability}
PyGeoParallax-IN (version 0.4.0, MIT licence), with the scripts and case lists used in this study, is archived on Zenodo \cite{pygeoparallax} (\url{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23812270}); the concept DOI \url{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23666957} resolves to the latest version. INSAT-3DR L1C and L2B products are available from MOSDAC, Space Applications Centre, ISRO (\url{https://www.mosdac.gov.in}); GPM DPR 2A Ku version 8 data from NASA GES DISC \cite{gpm2aku_v08}; ERA5 from the Copernicus Climate Data Store \cite{c3s2018}; SRTM \cite{farr2007} through OpenTopography; and coastlines from Natural Earth \cite{naturalearth}.

\section*{Acknowledgment}
INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR data were provided by MOSDAC, Space Applications Centre, ISRO. GPM data were provided by the NASA/JAXA Global Precipitation Measurement mission through NASA GES DISC. ERA5 was produced by ECMWF and made available by the Copernicus Climate Change Service. SRTM data were provided by NASA and USGS through OpenTopography, and coastlines by Natural Earth.
